title: Annotatio II §.I cont: Theological sense — doctrines necessary to faith and salvation; God alone fixes necessity
pass_a_gloss: OR IN THE THEOLOGICAL SENSE, and they are Doctrines altogether necessary both for constituting the Christian Religion or Faith and for attaining the End of the Christian Faith, the Salvation of our Souls, and thence commonly to be called, now Fundamentals of Faith, with respect to the Object, the intrinsic and essential Fundamentatum; now Fundamentals of Salvation, with respect to the End, the Fundamentatum partly intrinsic and essential, partly extrinsic and extra-essential being had. But with God alone in Holy Scripture determining all the necessity of these, and that either explicitly or implicitly, by a consequence obvious to anyone; and likewise in an exclusive Sense no less than a positive, so that God both may say which Doctrines are Necessary, and may will those not said by him to be Necessary, whether explicitly or implicitly, by that very fact exempted from the Necessity of Faith and Salvation, yet not equally from Utility of various Degree. For it is neither probable, nor in any way to be admitted, that God, held indeed as the sole Author of the whole of Holy Scripture, in which both things Necessary to Faith and Salvation and less necessary things are handed down promiscuously, and some necessary things are also now and then openly signified, should be believed either not to have defined all necessary things in any way, and so not to have sufficiently distinguished the necessary from the less necessary, or to have left this definition and distinction to human arbitrium; especially since he has handed down promiscuously all things necessary to salvation, and therefore as such. See these things more fully taught in the Inquisition into the Arminians, Annotation XVII.
pass_b_english: Or take fundamentals in the theological sense: doctrines wholly necessary both to constitute Christian religion or faith and to reach faith's end — the salvation of our souls.

Hence they are commonly called either fundamentals of faith (toward the object: the intrinsic, essential thing founded) or fundamentals of salvation (toward the end: the thing founded partly intrinsic/essential, partly extrinsic/extra-essential).

God alone in Holy Scripture fixes all that necessity — explicitly or implicitly, by a consequence open to anyone — and in an exclusive sense no less than a positive one: so God both names which doctrines are necessary and, by not naming others as necessary (explicitly or implicitly), exempts them from faith-and-salvation necessity, though not from usefulness of every degree.

It is neither likely nor admissible that God, sole author of all Scripture — where necessities for faith and salvation are mixed with lesser matters, and some necessities are at times marked openly — either failed to define all necessities at all (and so failed to distinguish them from the less necessary) or left that definition and distinction to human whim; especially since he handed down everything needed for salvation promiscuously, and as such. See this taught more fully in the Inquisition into the Arminians, Annotation XVII.
source_text: VEL SENSU THEOLOGICO, & sunt Doctrinae, tam ad Religionem vel Fidem Christianam constituendam, quàm ad Fidei Christianae Finem, Animarum nostrarum Salutem consequendam, omninò necessariae, indeque communiter dicendae, modò Fundamentales Fidei, respectu ad Objectum, Fundamentato intrinsecum & essentiale; modò Fundamentales Salutis, respectu ad Finem, Fundamentato partim intrinsecum & essentialem, partim extrinsecum & extraessentialem, habito. Necessitatem autem istarum omnem determinante, in Scriptura S., Deô solô, idque vel explicitè, vel implicitè, per obviam cuivis consequentiam; itemque exclusivo non minus Sensu, quàm positivo, ut & dicat Deus, quaenam Necessariae Doctrinae sint; & non dictas ab eo Necessarias, sive explicitè, sive implicitè, eô ipsô à Necessitate Fidei & Salutis, non tamen pariter à varii Gradûs Utilitate, exemptas velit. Neque enim vel probabile est, vel ullo modo admittendum, ut Deus, universae Scripturae S. unicus quidem Autor habitus, in qua & Necessaria ad Fidem Salutemque, & minus necessaria promiscuè traduntur, necessaria etiam nonnulla subindè apertè significantur, vel non omnia necessaria ullo modo definivisse, sicque necessaria à minus necessariis non satis distinxisse, vel definitionem distinctionemque hanc humano arbitrio permisissse credendus sit; praesertim cùm cuncta, ad salutem necessaria, promiscuè, eóque ut talia, tradiderit. Vide haec fusius edocta Inquisit. in Arminian. Annot. XVII.
